system.description:
Aarakocra are intelligent bird-people. They live in small tribes of about 11-30, each with a hunting territory of about 10,000 square miles, on high mountain peaks where they can soar all day on the winds and thermals.

Relations: they have little to do with humans beyond the occasional theft of a farm animal (they cannot seem to tell domestic animals from wild ones, so this is not done out of malice). They have even less to do with demi-humans, and actively dislike humanoids. Now and then an aarakocra may agree to give information to humans, or scout for them, in exchange for shiny coins or gems. They hate to leave their own mountains, so this very rarely happens outside the bird-man’s territory.

Build: an aarakocra stands about 5’ tall with a 20’ wingspan. The wings work like a pterodactyl’s, with a hand halfway along each leading edge; beyond the hand, a greatly lengthened and strengthened outer finger forms the wing’s edge and locks in place in flight. These wing-hands cannot grasp while flying, but with the wings folded on the ground they are nearly as useful as human hands (three normal-sized fingers and an opposable thumb). The huge wing muscles attach to a bony keel that juts a full foot further forward than a human chest. The legs are powerful, with backward-bending knees and dangerous-looking talons. The feet are worse than they look: the talons can unlock and fold back to reveal a second pair of working hands, each with three tough, strong fingers and a thumb.

Combat:

  • Javelins: in the air the aarakocra fights with these lower hands, using the talons alone or gripping heavy fletched javelins for stabbing or throwing. Each warrior usually carries six, strapped to its chest in separate sheaths; each does 2-8 hit points of damage. They throw them in flight with none of the usual to-hit penalties for aerial missile fire. A bird-man keeps its last javelin for stabbing rather than throw it away.
  • Diving attack: its deadliest attack is a fast dive with a javelin in each lower hand, pulling out just as it reaches the target and driving both javelins into the victim with great force while giving a blood-curdling shriek. This attack is +4 to hit and does double damage, but needs at least 200’ of dive.
  • Bite: the beak can bite for 1-3 hit points, but is rarely used unless the bird-man is trapped on the ground.
  • Flight: like eagles, they can plunge a long way straight down and pull out at the last moment. They are manoeuvrability class C in aerial combat.
  • Fragility: though strong, they are light (adults typically weigh 50-80 pounds) and avoid ground melee or anything that could lead to grappling, since their hollow bones are fragile and could break if, for instance, a bird-man were thrown hard to the ground.

Claustrophobia: aarakocra are extremely claustrophobic. They will not even enter buildings, and only a mad or desperate bird-man would go underground.

Society: aarakocra lay eggs, which the females tend through an 8-month incubation. These nest-bound females make all the tribe’s javelins, tools, and other small items; the males do nothing but hunt. The females also weave the brilliant feathered banners and pennants that fly over the tribal nest and mark its territory (each tribe has its own distinctive design). They weave lying on their backs and using all four hands at once, an impressive sight. Each hand is less dextrous than a human’s, but the extra pair more than makes up for it. The bird-men are known to have tribal shamans.

Languages and allies: they speak their own language and that of giant eagles, with whom they are on terms of mutual respect; 10% also speak common. They get on very well with all air elementals. Any five aarakocra can summon an air elemental by chanting and flying an intricate aerial dance (taking three melee rounds). The elemental does what they ask as a favour, but will not fight to the death for them; it returns to its own plane (if it can) before that could happen.

Appearance: plumage colour varies by tribe, but males are always crested and gaudier than females, especially in the once-yearly mating season. The beak is about 5” long, grey-black, shaped somewhere between a parrot’s and an eagle’s. The face is not at all human, though the eyes face forward for binocular vision, and their sight is keen enough to make out detail at great distances.

Each aarakocra can carry up to 1,500 g.p. weight (150 pounds).

system.hd: Body 40 hits points; legs 15 hit points each
system.description:
Why these foul birds were first summoned from the infernal regions has been forgotten, but survivors of the original flock still haunt shadowy places and underground passages. An achaierai is a huge round head-body, with a powerful beak and feathery crest, on four long legs ending in strong claws.

Combat:

  • Man-sized opponents usually cannot reach the soft body, only the hard, metallic legs. Likewise the bird usually cannot reach them with its beak, so it fights with two claws for 1-8 hit points each. The claws always hit as a 4-dice monster.
  • When a beak attack is possible, it hits as a 9-dice monster and does 1-10 hit points.
  • Legs: 15 or more hit points of damage on one leg breaks it off. Losing one leg does not slow the bird; losing two halves its movement rate. An injured leg regenerates fully in about two days, but a leg completely lost does not grow back, and the bird has no other regenerative powers.
  • Morale: a group never needs to check morale, but any bird that loses a leg tries to flee. Though flightless (its stubby wings are barely visible and cannot support it), it often outruns pursuers on its long legs.
  • Toxic smoke: a bird that loses three legs, or is otherwise badly wounded, releases a cloud of black toxic smoke roughly a sphere of 10’ radius. Everyone in it (except achaierai) automatically takes 2-12 hit points of damage and must save against poison or go insane for 3 hours (treat as the druidic feeblemind spell with a limited duration). In the confusion the wounded bird tries to escape, crawling at a 2” movement rate if it has lost three legs.

Description: the legs are metallic blue-grey and the head-body dull scarlet with deep red blotches. The eyes are steel-blue and the wings blue-green. Many crest colours have been seen, the most common a bright flame-red.
system.hpNote: Claws always hit as a 4-dice monster; a beak attack, when one is possible, hits as a 9-dice monster. 15 or more damage on one leg breaks it off.

system.description:
This strange creature looks much like a mummy: man-sized, with loose folds of dirty white skin that at first glance look like a mummy’s bandages. It is not undead.

  • Fire: by coincidence, a resinous solvent in its body fluids makes it just as vulnerable to fire as a mummy (see the MM, Mummy).
  • Spells: it is immune to all 1st-level magic-user spells except magic missile, which does 3-18 hit points of damage to it per missile.
  • Adhesive skin: the skin constantly oozes a sour-smelling, very powerful glue. Anything but stone sticks to it, and only fire, boiling water, or the creature’s own voluntary secretions break the bond. Any weapon that hits it sticks fast (and does only half damage). Likewise, anyone it hits with its two-handed flailing fist attack (1-3 hit points) is stuck to it; its favourite tactic is to bind an opponent this way and use him as an unwilling shield. The glue stays sticky for 5-10 turns after the adherer dies.
  • Boiling liquid: a sizeable quantity of boiling water (or other boiling liquid) thrown over it does 1-3 hit points of damage and stops it sticking for the next melee round. The contents of a large bucket would just do, thrown from close enough to limit spreading.

Hunting: it usually waits in ambush, camouflaging itself by rolling in dirt, sticks, and leaves and carefully arranging larger debris to hide its shape. Any prey, of any size, passing near its hideout sets off its attack: it pounces on the closest target, trying to hit and cling with bulldog tenacity until the prey dies. If it is spotted and attacked (by missiles, or sometimes even loud noises) before any prey is in pouncing range, it becomes confused and hurriedly retreats.

It will attack almost anything given the chance, except spiders. It never attacks a spider of any kind, and has sometimes been known to work with them to trap prey.

An aleax is the physical form of certain gods’ vengeance. Each such god has only one, sent to punish and redeem those who stray from their alignment, fail to sacrifice enough treasure, or otherwise anger the god. An aleax is never met by chance.

Appearance: it takes human form, closely resembling its intended victim. To the victim it appears bathed in shimmering light whose colour depends on the god’s alignment: golden for lawful good, deep purple for lawful evil, ever-changing rose-and-blue for chaotic good, and so on. As it appears, it speaks a few brief words in the victim’s alignment language saying the victim is to be punished by his god. Otherwise it never speaks, under any pressure.

The fight: it attacks its victim at once. No one else can detect it in any way, and no physical or magical attack touches it except the victim’s; to onlookers the victim seems to be fighting a completely invisible, invulnerable being. To the victim it is his own exact duplicate in every way not stated otherwise: same characteristics, hit points, armour, weapons, and so on. There are only two differences in combat:

  1. Regeneration: after it is first wounded, it regenerates 1 hit point the next round, then 2, then 4, then 8, and so on, until it is killed (reduced to zero hit points or below) or fully healed. If it is hit again after that, the progression restarts at 1.
  2. Critical hits: a hit on it with an unmodified roll of 19 does double damage, and with an unmodified 20 quadruple damage. (The aleax’s own damage to its victim is normal, whatever its to-hit roll.)

If the victim dies: he loses all his treasure (even hidden caches; gods are nearly all-knowing) and half his experience points. He is then automatically raised and starts again at the matching experience level. All his magic items lose their properties: scrolls go blank, potions inert, and so on. No resurrection is needed, and no further aleax visits him as long as he stays true to his god from then on.

If the victim kills the aleax: he is taken to Heaven (or Olympus, Hell, Valhalla, as appropriate) to serve his god in person for a year and a day. On his return he regains all his former possessions (which here keep their properties and powers, though no other character can use them while he is away), and the deity will almost certainly (95% chance) add an extra reward, such as a powerful magic item or promotion to the next experience level, at the referee’s discretion.
system.hpNote: An aleax has exactly the hit points of the victim it was sent for (FF p.11).

system.specialDefenses: Immune to edged weapons of less than +2 bonus
system.magicResistance: Immune to fireballs and lightning; otherwise standard
system.description:
An algoid looks like a green humanoid with coarse, rough features, but it is really a colony of algae that, gathered in this form, has gained some mobility and a crude intelligence. The form is only temporary.

  • Attacks: two powerful fists, each doing 1-10 hit points of damage. It can also deliver one mind blast per day.
  • Defences: it is immune to psionic attacks. Edged weapons pass through it harmlessly unless they are +2 or better, in which case they do half damage. Blunt weapons, magical or not, do full damage. It is immune to certain magical attacks (fireball, lightning), but especially vulnerable to part water and lower water, each of which does 1-6 hit points of damage per experience level of the caster.
  • Tree control: like a treant (see the MM, Treant), it can control two trees of the kinds found near its home (swamp or lakeside pasture, always near water of some kind, stagnant or not), such as willows, water-oaks, cypresses, or similar trees. Controlled trees move at 3” and make two attacks per round for 1-10 hit points each.

The al-mi’raj usually roams pastures and woodlands, but is sometimes found in dungeons. Its lair is usually a small cave just below ground.

It looks like a large yellow hare with a long (1½’-2’) black horn sticking forward from the middle of its forehead, like a unicorn’s. In melee it stabs with the horn, and its nimbleness lets the horn do damage like a dagger (1-4 hit points).

It is not very bright and behaves unpredictably; it may well attack for no good reason. Captured young, it shows a surprising aptitude for training, and its fearlessness makes it a useful companion. It has a particularly keen sense of smell and sharp eyesight.

system.specialDefenses: Can only be hit by magical or silver weapons
system.description:
This ghastly undead creature exists mainly on the Ethereal Plane. It is turned as a spectre, and it is reluctant to approach mirrors or anything made of silver.

  • Sensing and surprise: an emotive sense lets it detect potential victims up to 100’ away. Because it appears so uncannily out of a wall, floor, or ceiling, it surprises on 1-5 (d6), and uses the surprise to close in on its victim. When seen, it looks like an insubstantial skeletal figure in a thin white robe.
  • Its “attack”: it cannot attack physically, but its chosen victim feels bony, claw-like fingers at the throat, even through armour. No to-hit roll is needed. Even if the victim knows it cannot really hurt him, the suggestion is immensely strong:
    1. The victim rolls 3d6. A total under his intelligence means the suggestion fails, and he is immune to that particular apparition.
    2. A total equal to or above his intelligence means he is stricken with horror and rolls 3d6 again, against his constitution. Under his constitution, he flees in terror for 1-4 melee rounds (and can be attacked again while fleeing).
    3. Equal to or above his constitution, he suffers a massive heart seizure and dies instantly.
  • The slain: a victim killed this way can be raised, but if the body is left, or no attempt to raise it is made within one hour, it rises as an apparition in 2-8 hours.
  • Hitting it: characters able to move and fight on the Ethereal Plane can attack it normally there. It stays on the Prime Material Plane for only one melee round per victim attacked, and only then can non-ethereal means harm it; during its attack it can be hit, as AC 0, by magical or silver weapons.

Assassin bugs look like giant bluebottle flies with four small limbs, tiny arms and legs. They are rarely seen except in their mating season (one day in every two months), when a male and female may be met flying in search of a host for their young. The natural host is human, but they have been known to lay eggs in demi-humans and (rarely) humanoids.

  • The male always attacks first, biting for 1-4 hit points, while the female flies nearby, as close to the victim as she can without risking attack. If the bite succeeds, its saliva paralyses the bitten area unless the victim saves at +2. The male keeps attacking until destroyed. In aerial combat they are manoeuvrability class C.
  • The female detects the scent of the male’s saliva. As soon as one of his bites has caused paralysis, she “attacks” the paralysed area; if she succeeds, she implants her egg in the victim’s body, and then dies.
  • The egg hatches 13-24 hours after implanting, producing 7-12 larvae. Until then only a very powerful spell, such as limited wish or heal, will remove or kill it.
  • The larvae each do 1 hit point of damage to the host every hour as they devour its internal organs. After 2 weeks they leave, burrowing out through the spot where the egg was implanted and doing another 5-8 hit points each as they go. Once outside, they change into fully grown assassin bugs.

Killing the larvae: while the larvae are inside, these spells cast on the host will help:

  • Cure serious wounds: kills one larva per experience level of the caster above 6th.
  • Cure critical wounds: kills all larvae.
  • Heal: kills all larvae and restores all but 5-8 of the victim’s hit points.
  • A limited wish or similar spell can also work during this period.

Trolls, troglodytes, and bugbears consider assassin bug eggs a great delicacy. The eggs are oval, 4-5” long, and deep blue.

Description: assassin bugs are generally the colour of bluebottle flies, the female usually a lighter shade than the male. The four limbs are the colour of human flesh. The wings are almost transparent with a faint silver tint.

Astral searchers are mindless shells of hazy humanoid shape, created by concentrated or traumatic human thought. Violent death, spells cast on the Astral Plane, and astral combat often create them (without their creator or source ever knowing). Driven by their past link with material beings, they seek material bodies with complete single-mindedness.

Crossing over: they wander the Astral Plane looking for weak points in the fabric between the Astral and Prime Material Planes, and gather there, waiting for the stress lines to line up so they can pass through the resulting gaps. Such weak points occur naturally, and can also be created temporarily by astral travel (4% chance).

Attack: once on the Prime Material Plane, they attack the nearest living humanoids, hoping to possess their bodies. They attack the mind, so every victim counts as AC 5 against them, whatever his physical or magical protection. Victims believe the attack is physical and take damage accordingly, but all of it is illusory and fades 3-12 rounds after the searchers’ attack ends.

Possession: if a searcher brings its victim to zero hit points or below, the victim’s mind and personality are destroyed and the searcher takes the body. It gains the victim’s physical abilities and hit points (since all damage from its attack now disappears), but not his personality; roll a new alignment at random. The body becomes a new non-player character in a player character’s body, and the referee decides what it does, taking its alignment into account.

  • A searcher can be exorcised, but the original mind has been completely destroyed and the player character cannot be raised or brought back. An emptied body is an open invitation to possession by a demon or similar creature (at the referee’s discretion).
  • They can be attacked physically; destroying the materialised body destroys and disperses the searcher itself.
  • Because they exist on two planes at once, they are 50% resistant to magic.
  • They are not undead in any way.

Babblers are strange mutations of lizard men: large, heavy marsh-dwellers that native tribes near their swamps call marsh-gibberers. They are mostly dirty yellow with grey undersides, and mottled grey patches form strange patterns on their muscular bodies. A babbler is shaped like a small gorgosaurus, with a tough, flexible tail that keeps it steady when upright.

  • Movement: it normally slithers on its stomach at a surprisingly fast 12” rate. To fight it must stand upright, slowing to 6”.
  • Attacks: two foreclaws (1-6 hit points each) and a bite (1-8 hit points) from its particularly large mouth full of rows of sharp teeth.
  • Stealth: moving on its belly it is hard to detect (25% chance), though animals smell it from some distance. If it approaches unnoticed, it can strike from behind as a 4th-level thief, at +4 to hit and for double damage.

Babblers are particularly fond of human flesh and attack humans unless outnumbered more than two to one. Raiding parties of marsh lizard men have been seen led by one, two, or even three babblers, hunting human flesh.

They speak among themselves in a babbling near-language that humans have failed to analyse or learn, and they understand the common tongue in a basic way.

system.xp: I/5 + 1 per hit point or I/10 + 1 per hit point
system.description:
Giant bats are huge versions of the meat-eating kind of ordinary bat, with bodies 3’ long and a 5’-6’ wingspan. They live in dark caverns, usually underground. In flight they make a high-pitched whistle that guides them and makes up for their poor eyesight.

  • Agility: they are very nimble fliers. Anyone with dexterity under 13 shooting a missile at a flying giant bat is −3 to hit. They are manoeuvrability class C in aerial combat.
  • Bite: a bat must land, usually on its victim, to bite (1-2 or 1-4 points of damage). 1% of victims bitten catch rabies.
  • Only 10% of giant bats are of the 1 hit die kind.
system.hpNote: Only 10% of giant bats are of the 1 hit die kind (FF p.14).

system.description:
The berbalang is a solitary biped with leathery skin and bat-like wings. Its eyes are white and watery, and its infravision reaches twice as far as an elf’s (120’).

Astral life: it spends most of each month apparently dormant, hibernating, preferably in a well-hidden cave. Though it seems to be in a coma, it is really roaming the Astral Plane, hunting and killing weaker creatures and carrying out bizarre, complex courtship and mating rituals with other berbalangs. If its body is found and disturbed, it tries to return and animate it, but this can take a long time (1-100 rounds) depending on how far across the planes it is. If the body is destroyed, the astral berbalang dies too, so it is very careful and very clever about hiding itself.

The projection: for three days each month, at the full moon, it returns to its body, changes its kind of trance, and sends a physical projection of itself onto the Prime Material Plane to look for food: a freshly killed human corpse.

  • The projection is a duplicate of the original that can take and deal damage. The berbalang uses all its senses and directs it (in effect it is the projection) in its search for food. It can range up to 3 miles from the body.
  • If it must fight, it fights as the berbalang does: two claws (1-4 hit points each) and a bite (1-6 hit points). The berbalang and its projection are both manoeuvrability class B in aerial combat.
  • Wounded: if it takes damage it flees at once, flying back (24” rate) to the body, which cannot project again for as many days as the hit points lost.
  • Killed: it disappears, and there is a 75% chance the original also dies of system shock.
  • Not fed: if the projection is driven back, or destroyed, before it feeds, a new one goes out as soon as possible (after the required recovery time), whatever the phase of the moon.
  • Feeding: when it kills a human, it picks up the body and flies at full speed back to the host, which immediately wakes from its trance. It feeds on the body in flight and can devour a fully grown human in one turn, leaving only bones, clothes, and equipment.

Revenge: a berbalang that survives an attack eventually seeks revenge on its attacker, though this may wait until its body recovers. Those who follow a wounded projection back to the lair may be surprised to meet the unwounded physical creature.

Habits: to avoid exhausting its food supply or causing too much local alarm, a berbalang moves its body to a new area every three or four months. They always travel by night and avoid confrontations when physically present. They live on the edge of civilisation, where lack of organisation gives them free rein, so one is very rarely met in physical form unless adventurers find its lair or follow its projection back to it.

How the berbalang gets nourishment when only its projection feeds, and how it reproduces when all mating takes place on the Astral Plane, remain unexplained.

This underground creature is a yellow, frog-like humanoid with huge eyes that shine like searchlights.

  • Eye beams: at rest it keeps its eyes “turned off” with an extra eyelid, but it can “attack” instantly by opening them, and its keen hearing usually tells it which way its target is. Anyone in its beams within 30’ must save (as against wands) or be blinded for 11-20 turns. Anyone with infravision within that range saves at −3.
  • Armour class: those not blinded still cannot look straight at it, so its effective armour class is 1. Against an attacker immune to bright light for any reason, its true armour class is 3.
  • Bite: at close quarters it bites viciously for 1-8 hit points of damage.

It is various shades of yellow, darker on its back and lighter on its belly. The eyes of a dead blindheim, if opened, are a dull gold.

Blood hawks are like normal hawks only in size: their beaks are razor sharp and their talons unusually strong. Their eagle-like wings make them fast fliers, manoeuvrability class B in aerial combat.

They swoop swiftly and silently onto their victims, attacking with the beak (1-6 hit points) and two sets of talons (1-4 hit points each). They love human flesh and keep attacking humans even when a fight is going against them. They pick at the bodies of their prey, not just for food but for gems, which they use to line their nests to attract females. They ignore all other kinds of treasure.

A blood hawk is a uniform medium grey.

Giant bloodworms usually live in shallow pools in underground caverns. They cannot swim, but push themselves along the bottom or on nearby firm ground. Their underside is dark, slimy brown and their top mottled green; lying half in and half out of a pool in dim light, one is easily mistaken for a moss-covered boulder.

  • It attacks only when hungry (it eats once a week) or when stepped on.
  • Attack: it tries to fasten its large sucker mouth onto a victim. This first attack needs a to-hit roll and does no damage. After that it drains blood automatically every round, with no to-hit roll, for 1-8 hit points, until it dies or lets go.
  • Fire: it takes double damage from all fire attacks and saves at −2 against magical fire. Short of killing it, a successful fire attack is the only way to make it let go, and if it survives it tries to reattach immediately.

The bonesnapper is a small descendant of a long-extinct kind of meat-eating dinosaur, as stupid as it is aggressive. It always fights to the death. In melee it bites with its large, sharp-toothed jaws (1-8 hit points) and at the same time sweeps its tail at the same victim (1-4 hit points).

Though non-intelligent, it has an ancient instinct to collect human bones, especially jawbones, to decorate its underground lair. The number of bones in a lair is a good sign of the owner’s standing among its kind.

Description: grey-green, mottled with dark grey spots and patches, with tiny scarlet eyes and yellow-white teeth.

Booka are sprite-like creatures that like to live in attics, under eaves, and on sunny rooftops. They hate the cold, and in cold climates always stay indoors near chimneys. On bright, sunny mornings they sweep the stairs or porch of the house they live in, always when no one is around to see. If disturbed at this, they become angry and move out at once.

  • Abilities: they are very fast and can also fly (manoeuvrability class A), and can turn invisible at will, even while running or flying. They avoid combat of any kind by using invisibility if at all possible.
  • Tricks: they hate evil creatures and play tricks on them when they can: hiding valued objects, tangling rope, hair, clothing, and so on, and generally causing trouble.
  • Revenge: if a booka is captured or harmed in any way, any others who know of it will certainly bring dozens more to cause mischief until the offender frees the captive or makes amends with a valuable gift (a sack of gold, jewellery, or even something magical), left on a rooftop for a day. Angry booka who are not appeased eventually cause some fatal accident, setting snares and traps for the offender.

A booka is only about 1’ tall. Males and females alike tend to have large features and thin bodies; “homely” is the kindest word for them.

system.treasure: J, K, M, Q (x5) & C (magic only) in lair
system.xp: Regular = I/18 + 1 per hit point; Leader = II/36 + 2 per hit point; Shaman or Great Chief = III/80 + 3 per hit point
system.description:
Bullywugs are a race of upright, frog-like monsters that live in wet places: rainy forests, marshes, damp caves, or almost anywhere shady or dark with water nearby, since they must wet their skins from time to time.

Two kinds: some groups are more intelligent than others. The intelligent ones tend to live in caves or deserted human buildings and usually have armour, shields, and various weapons (use human bandits as a guide). The less advanced bullywugs hate their brighter kin and make war on them.

Movement and attacks:

  • Without armour and shield a bullywug swims fast; even with them it swims at 9”. Armoured or not, it can hop 3” forward or 1½” up.
  • Hopping attack: their normal way of fighting is to hop to the attack with a weapon, gaining +1 on the to-hit roll(s); with an impaling weapon, a successful hopping attack does double damage. A weapon can be set against a hop just as against a charge (which, in effect, it is). Bullywugs without weapons, or disarmed, still hop to the attack, using two claws (1-2 hit points each) and a bite (2-5 hit points).
  • Weakness: unless using long weapons, they always attack after their opponents, because they move slowly or are exposed while hopping.
  • Camouflage: they can change skin colour, like a chameleon, to grey, green, or brown in light or dark shades. Motionless in suitable surroundings, a bullywug is 75% unlikely to be noticed, even by infravision (the colour change alters body heat too). Attacking unnoticed from camouflage, it surprises on 3 in 6 (5 in 6 if hopping to the attack).

Leaders: bullywugs form organised bands, always led by a large individual with a full 8 hit points.

  • 30 or more: at least 5 large individuals, and a leader of 10-13 hit points (effectively a 2-dice monster) who does +1 damage on all attacks.
  • Groups using armour etc. have a 10% chance per ten bullywugs of a tribal shaman of 11-14 hit points.
  • 60 or more: a great chief of 16-19 hit points who does +2 damage on all attacks.

Relations: they readily serve chaotic evil masters, human or not. Rumour says bullywug-human crossbreeds are possible, and that certain degenerate humans live in mixed communities with them, serving nameless things from caverns deep underground. Sahuagin despise them and occasionally raid a bullywug lair for sport and out of sheer malice, eating any captives alive. Lizard men rarely associate with bullywugs, though they are not openly hostile.

Bullywugs have their own rather primitive language, and the more intelligent ones can speak common haltingly, with a limited vocabulary.
system.hpNote: The leader of 10-13 hit points is effectively a 2-dice monster (FF p.17).

system.description:
The bunyip is a water beast like a seal with thick black fur, a black mane, and unusually powerful jaws. It lives in lakes, marshes, and slow rivers.

  • Playful but strong: it is mischievous rather than hostile, but big and strong enough to tip over a small boat.
  • Roar: it can sense approaching humans and may (50% chance) rise briefly above the surface to roar at a nearby party. Every party member below 4th experience level must save at −2 against wands or flee in panic.
  • Bite: if a small creature such as a dwarf is struggling in the water, it usually (80% chance) bites, trying to sever and swallow a limb. It does not attack anything bigger than a dwarf except in self-defence, or if the victim is already bleeding. A bite does 1-6 hit points; on a to-hit roll of 20, a limb is severed (chosen at random or by the circumstances).

This small creature is like an armadillo, with an “armoured” back of small interlocking plates of tough, leathery skin, attractively patterned in shades of brown; its underside is light grey flecked with small green patches. It eats only leaves and small insects and is rarely found outside places with plenty of them, such as woods and marshes.

The ruby: a large ruby is set in its head just above the eyes. It is part of the animal; if the carbuncle dies, the ruby shatters into worthless dust. A wizard (or anyone of equal standing) using a charm monster or charm animal ability can coax it into giving the ruby up.

  • Value: usually (70%) 500 gp; rarer ones (25%) have 1,000 gp gems; 5% have a 5,000 gp gem.
  • A removed gem regrows at 100 gp per month, and its value may change each time it regrows.

Mind: it has empathy and telepathy (it communicates by telepathy), and slight powers of prophecy about the immediate future. Its empathy lets it understand the character of everyone it meets and know what they know, though it is not intelligent enough to form more than very basic ideas.

Behaviour: if attacked it does not resist and is easily captured, but it can will itself to die; it has no fear or idea of death and gives up its life if put under pressure. It usually approaches a party, tells them telepathically what its gem is worth, and tries to join them. Once it has gained their trust, its malicious nature takes over: it uses selective telepathy and prophecies, true and false, to stir up hostility, suspicion, and even fighting within the group. Rarely, it may instead secretly enrage nearby monsters into attacking the party. Its motives are unclear, but some sages believe that because it cannot understand death, it is fascinated by combat and especially by death, and does its utmost to bring them about. Once it succeeds, it watches in morbid fascination, then slips quietly away at a good moment.

Caryatid columns are much like stone golems (see the MM, Golem, Stone). They are made using a magical tome, or by a magic-user of 16th level or higher using the same spells as for a stone golem, but they cost slightly more and take twice as long because they are so intricate.

Appearance: the result is a slim, decorative stone pillar about 7’ tall. At a glance it is just ornamental stonework, perhaps one of an identical pair on either side of the entrance to a chamber, chapel, or throne-room. Closer inspection shows it is not symmetrical around its length but has the very slender shape of a woman. Once that is noticed, it becomes clear that one of her hands, held close to her side, holds a slim sword that blends so smoothly into the stone it is nearly invisible.

Purpose: a caryatid column always has a specific guarding task (it is never met as a wandering monster), set by its creator: guarding a treasure chest, keeping intruders out of an area, or similar. If the creator is nearby when it animates, it can be controlled with simple spoken commands; more often the creator is absent, and it follows simple courses of action the creator set in advance.

Animating: it comes to life as soon as anyone does what its task forbids, such as a thief approaching the treasure or an intruder entering the forbidden area. It then takes on a fleshy look, shrinks to about 5½’, and fills out slightly into the shape of a fair young maiden. The stone sword becomes steel.

  • Avoiding a fight: it does not necessarily fight. Its main aim is its task, and if it can do that without combat it tries to. Its behaviour depends a great deal on circumstances and its creator’s instructions; it might, for example, lure intruders away from the forbidden area into a trap, a monster, or spell attack from its creator.
  • Combat: if combat is unavoidable, it strikes first. It strikes as a 5 HD creature with its sword for 2-8 hit points of damage.
  • Weapons against it: normal weapons do half damage; magical weapons do full damage but without their magical bonus. Any weapon, magical or not, that hits it has a 25% chance (not cumulative) of snapping, less 5% per “plus” (a +4 sword has a 5% chance). Magical weapons with no plus count as +1.

When its task is done (intruders killed, treasure no longer at risk, for example), it returns to its place and turns back to stone, sword and all. If killed, it turns back to stone (as does the sword) where it falls.

The caterwaul is a solitary, vicious, two-legged cat-like predator with short midnight-blue fur, yellow eyes, and a long tail. Its lair is usually a cave strewn with twigs and rushes, its walls covered in deep scratch marks where it sharpens its claws. Its treasure is only shiny objects, and it especially likes gems.

It has an uncanny natural agility that varies between individuals. Roll percentile dice for each one encountered:

  • Armour class bonus: this dexterity bonus also applies to dodging and to saving throws against fireball, lightning bolt, and the like.

Movement and senses: it moves fast on two legs and can reach top speed (24” rate) in short bursts by dropping to all fours. It can climb almost any surface (base 5% chance of slipping), move silently (75%), and hide in shadows (75%), so it prefers to lurk high up and spring down on unsuspecting prey. Its keen hearing and exceptional sense of smell make it hard to surprise (10% chance).

Attacks: two claws (1-4 hit points each) and a bite (1-6 hit points) each round, or more often as the table shows. Its first attack (and only that one) always comes with a high-pitched, keening screech that does 1-8 hit points of damage to everyone within 60’ who hears it; a save against breath means no damage.

system.specialDefenses: Damage from edged weapons reduced - see below
system.description:
The cifal (the name stands for “colonial insect-formed artificial life”) is several swarms of insects, each of several hundred thousand, that come together as a single shapeless, roughly man-sized creature.

  • Hit dice: the mass has 8 hit dice, plus another 2 hit dice of energy that holds the swarms together in one body. Damage comes off the binding 2 hit dice first. If those hit points are lost, the body breaks up into its separate insects, which fly away at 24” (they attack and defend only as a mass). The mass can replace binding hit points from its other hit points at 2 per melee round.
  • Attack: a mass of tiny bites doing 1-12 hit points in all.
  • Weapons: edged weapons do only 1 hit point of damage, whatever the weapon and whether magical or not. Blunt weapons do full normal damage.
  • Movement: strictly, it does not fly; its movement rate is along the ground, though it comes from the swarms’ flying speed held back by the need to keep their shape. The cifal has no aerial manoeuvrability class, but its individual insects are class A.
system.hpNote: Damage comes off the binding force first; when it is gone the mass breaks up into insects. The mass body can move 2 hit points per round back into the binding force (FF p.19).

system.description:
Clubneks are mutated ostriches with hard, bony beaks that do 1-8 hit points of damage; they also fight with two claws for 1-6 hit points each. One melee round in every five, they can put on a burst of speed and move at 24”.

They are various shades of green with yellow beaks. They are not normally aggressive unless threatened, but their behaviour is erratic and unpredictable. They normally eat plants and are rarely found underground, preferring to roam meadows and woods.

system.specialDefenses: Can only be hit by magical weapons
system.description:
These foul undead are found in stranded funeral barges, or wherever a corpse has failed to return to its maker. Though it looks like a zombie, it is treated as a wraith on the cleric/undead table. Sleep, charm, and other mind-affecting spells do not affect it.

  • False death: normal weapons seem to hurt it, but do not actually do any damage. If it takes more than 6 hit points from normal weapons in one melee round, it falls down, apparently finished; the next round it rises and fights on, and everyone in melee with it must save against fear or flee in panic.
  • Magical weapons damage it normally, with their usual bonus.
  • Attack: occasionally (25%) it has a weapon it uses in combat. Otherwise it attacks bare-handed (a single attack for 1-6 hit points). A bare-handed hit means it has locked its hands around the victim’s throat, and each round after that it does 1-6 hit points automatically (no to-hit roll) until it or the victim dies. Nothing will break its grip once locked.

Crabmen are amphibious creatures usually found in seashore caves. They are humanlike in shape, with a hard reddish-brown shell, and have two pincers instead of hands, each doing 1-4 hit points of damage in combat.

They value silver highly and go to any lengths to get it, even attacking a character they suspect is carrying something made of it. Normally they are quite peaceful, but now and then an instinct drives them out of their coastal homes on a savage raid inland, in bands of 30 or 40, looting everything in their path and attacking anyone who resists.

Sahuagin often raid crabmen, whom they consider a tasty delicacy. However, the sahuagin’s usual net-throwing tactics fail against crabmen, whose pincers cut through nets very quickly.

The crypt thing is a pale, solitary skeletal being that always wears a brown hooded robe. It stays in its lair permanently (at least, none has been met anywhere else) and does not attack if left alone.

Teleport: its special power is an unfailing, improved form of teleport that it casts on a party (once per party encountered). Everyone who fails a saving throw is instantly teleported, rolling percentile dice for each victim separately:

d100Distance and direction
01-20100-1000’ north
21-40100-1000’ south
41-60100-1000’ east
61-80100-1000’ west
81-90one dungeon level up
91-00one dungeon level down

Victims never arrive inside solid material; if the target spot is solid, they arrive in the nearest open space, though not necessarily at floor level.

Combat: those who save may attack it, but only magical weapons can hit it. It fights back with a two-handed clawing attack for 1-8 hit points of damage.

It can speak the neutral tongue, but if asked where missing party members went, it will not reveal its power and insists they were disintegrated.

There are rumoured to be aberrant crypt things that paralyse victims and turn them invisible at the same time, instead of teleporting them. Neither kind feeds on its victims; both seem to want only the pleasure of causing confusion and dissent.

The dakon is a shabby, intelligent ape that speaks the common tongue reasonably well. It never attacks except in self-defence or to recover treasure stolen from it. When it does, its strength and sharp claws give it +2 to hit, and each claw does 1-10 hit points of damage.

It is usually light brown, with green eyes and black hands, and is found anywhere except near large expanses of water. It is normally on good terms with lawful humans and near-humans, but it distrusts the motives of humanoids and will not talk to them.

“Dark creeper” is a folk name; the race’s own name is unknown and its language is beyond linguists. It is a slightly built humanoid about the height of a dwarf, always dressed in sombre, dark clothes that hide as much of its pale skin as possible. Dark creepers hate light and live deep underground, usually alone, though there are rumours of underground villages of as many as 80, including 20%-25% females, always ruled by a dark stalker.

Treasure: they are especially fond of small magic items such as rings and magic daggers. A lone creeper carries 25% of its treasure in the deep pockets of its cloak, so each one met has a 15% chance of a magic dagger, a 5% chance of a magic ring, and a 10% chance of 1-4 gems or 1-2 pieces of jewellery. In a lair, multiply these chances by the number of males living there, and add 1-100 platinum pieces and 50-500 gold pieces.

Abilities: a creeper has the abilities of a 4th-level thief and can detect magic items within 15’. It attacks with a dagger (magical, if it has one).

Darkness: three times a day it can create darkness. All torches, lanterns, and other non-magical lights within 50’ go out and cannot be relit for the next hour (the power’s duration). Even infravision is useless in it.

  • Magical lights save against magical frost; on a failure they go out for the hour and then return to normal.
  • Spells such as light can counter it.
  • The creeper does not use it against parties without artificial light, so, for instance, elves relying on infravision usually pass unbothered.
  • During the darkness it has two aims: first, to destroy lanterns and tinderboxes, break flasks of oil, and do anything else that will stop light being made; second, to steal any small magic items it detected. Staying alive ranks just above both.

Attacked in normal light, a creeper is AC 8.

Death: a slain creeper bursts into flame so intensely that everyone within 10’ is blinded for 1-6 full turns (saving roll against magic allowed). Every trace of the creeper is destroyed, though metal items are usually (80% chance) unharmed. Magic items, metal or not, lose their magic if they fail a save against magical fire.

Dark stalkers are the rarely seen leaders of the dark creepers. They are almost a separate race, breeding nearly always among themselves, and are easy to spot in a group of creepers since they are man-sized and stand head and shoulders above them. There is about one stalker for every 25 creepers, and every creeper village has at least one stalker ruler. They are seldom met alone, though this has happened while a stalker is on some mysterious personal mission.

  • Powers: all those of dark creepers, plus wall of fog twice per day.
  • Weapons: they fight with short swords if they must; 25% of these are magical.
  • Treasure: all of it is carried. Each one met has a 7% chance of a magic ring and a 12% chance of 2-5 gems or 1-2 pieces of jewellery.
  • Attacked in normal light, a dark stalker is AC 8.
  • Death: a slain stalker explodes in a blinding flash equal to a 3-dice fireball.

Death dogs are large, black, two-headed hounds whose heads attack independently. They usually hunt in packs in deserts or in dry places underground, and usually (85% chance) attack humans and near-humans on sight. They are said to be descended from Cerberus, and their loud, piercing double bark tends to support the idea.

  • Bite: each bite does 1-10 hit points. The victim must save against poison or die of a slow, rotting disease in 4-24 days; cure disease will cure it.
  • Knockdown: they usually go for the legs. A natural 19 or 20 to hit against a man-sized or smaller victim knocks him down; he attacks at −4 until he gets up, which takes a single round if he is not knocked down again.

Only twelve death knights are known to exist. Each is a horrifying kind of lich, made by a demon prince (thought to be Demogorgon) from a fallen human paladin.

  • Undead: it cannot be turned or dispelled (though holy word affects it), and it controls undead like a 6th-level cleric.
  • Magic resistance: 75%. In addition, a roll of 11 or lower on percentage dice reflects a spell back at its caster (roll each time a spell is tried).
  • Armour and strength: it wears light armour (9” or 12” movement depending on what else it carries) but is always armour class 0. It has 18(00) strength and usually fights with a sword (80% chance it is magical).
  • Steed: it usually rides a nightmare (see the MM, Nightmare). One can be summoned to serve it every ten years, serving as a paladin’s warhorse serves a paladin.
  • Constant powers: it radiates fear in a 5’ radius, can create a wall of ice at will, and has innate detect magic and detect invisibility.
  • Twice a day: dispel magic, and gating in a demon (75% chance the gate opens): type I (20%), type II (25%), type III (30%), type IV (20%), or type VI (5%).
  • Once a day: any one power word spell, a symbol of pain or fear, and a 20-dice fireball.
  • Its magic use, where it matters, is at the 20th experience level.

It speaks 3-6 languages besides its alignment tongue and common.

(*The X.P. value is for destroying her Material Plane form only; if she is actually killed permanently, multiply it by 10.)

Lolth is a very powerful and feared demon lord. On the Prime Material Plane she usually takes the form of a giant black widow spider, and sometimes does on her own plane too, but she also likes to appear as an exquisitely beautiful female dark elf (statistics for this form are given in parentheses). Little is known of her aims; only because drow worship makes her take form on the earth can much be learned about her at all.

Spiders: she enjoys the company of spiders of every kind: giant ones in her spider form, and normal, large, and even huge ones in her elf form. She can talk with all spiders, and they understand and obey her without question.

Durability: she has only 66 hit points, but her high armour class prevents most damage, and she can heal herself at will up to three times a day. Since she likes to roam in one form or another, she is seldom met in her lair on any plane, unless worshippers have called her to some special shrine or temple.

Spider form:

  • Webs: she casts web strands 30’ long from her spinnerets, equal to a web spell, with a poisonous coating that does 1-4 hit points per round to webbed victims.
  • Bite: in the same round she can bite for 4-16 hit points, plus death unless the victim saves against poison at −4.
  • Powers (one per melee round, at will): comprehend languages, confusion (creature looked at only), darkness (10’ radius), dispel magic, read magic, teleport with no inaccuracy, tongues, and true seeing. Twice a day: phase door and shape change. Once a day: gate in a demon (66% chance the gate opens) of type I (45%), type II (35%), or type III (20%), and summon 9-16 large (20%), 7-12 huge (30%), 2-8 giant (40%), or 1-4 phase (10%) spiders.

Elf form: she uses the weapons common to drow and is a 16th-level cleric/14th-level magic-user with matching abilities, but she cannot wear armour of any kind and loses her psionic powers.

Defences: non-magical weapons do not affect her, and silver does no harm unless magicked to at least +1. Cold, electricity, and gas do half damage. Acid, magic missiles (if her magic resistance fails), and poison affect her normally. Holy water is especially harmful: 6 points from a splash and 6-21 points (3d6 + 3) from a direct hit.

Senses: she sees into the infrared and ultraviolet to a normal distance of 120’, and has the limited telepathy of demons in general.

Psionics: body equilibrium, clairvoyance, domination, and the major sciences dimension walking, mind bar, molecular rearrangement, and probability travel. These, like her magical powers, are performed at 16th experience level.

Demons: general (FF)

These traits, common to all demons, are reprinted in edited form from the MM.

  • Planes: demons can move from their own plane to Tarterus, Hades, or Pandemonium, or roam the Astral Plane, but cannot enter the Material Plane without help (conjuration, a gate, speaking their name, or similar means). They often roam the Astral and Ethereal Planes, and people in an ethereal state attract their attention.
  • Nature: they are chaotic evil; the smarter and stronger rule the weaker and duller. The less intelligent attack without question and fight until slain. All can split their attacks between two or even three opponents if they have the means. No demon can ever be subdued.
  • Death: demons of type V and above are not really slain when their material form is killed; they are forced back to their home plane, to stay there for a century or until someone helps them come forth again. On their own plane, however, they can be slain.
  • Service: demons never serve willingly. Forced into service by magic or threat, they constantly look for a way to kill their master or captor. Those they take a liking to are usually carried off to their plane as (favoured) slaves. Characters of any alignment can summon demons, but controlling one is another matter entirely; a special pentacle is needed for type VI or greater. The DM must handle carefully the threat or reward a summoner uses to try to win a demon’s service. Demons are repelled by holy (good) relics or artifacts.
  • Names: if a particularly powerful demon’s name is spoken, he may hear and turn his attention to the speaker (a base 5% chance is recommended). Unless the speaker is ready to avoid this attention, or to control the demon, the demon will immediately kill him by the quickest means available.

Demons’ amulets: demon lords and princes keep their vital essence in small containers; their souls, in a sense, are both protected and vulnerable to any enterprising character who gets hold of the amulet.

  • Demons with amulets can magic jar once per day.
  • No magic can detect an amulet as such, and it looks ordinary in every way. The most powerful princes need not keep theirs with them, but lesser demons usually must carry theirs on or near them.
  • Holding a demon’s amulet gives power over that demon for, say, one adventure, and never more than a day (24 hours). Then the amulet must be returned, or it can be destroyed, banishing the prince to the abyss for a year (after which he can return only if summoned).
  • Using an amulet is very, very dangerous. Holding one doubles the chance of attracting another demon’s attention, and any demon not controlled by it attacks the holder at once. If the amulet leaves the hand of the person commanding its demon, that demon immediately attacks him in its most effective way, doing its utmost to kill him and carry everything that is left to its own domain; the character is lost forever.
  • On the other hand, if the holder carefully repays the demon for its help, adds a large sum for the nerve of commanding it at all, and then carefully returns the amulet, the prince might not hold a grudge forever or hunt him whenever possible.

The denzelian is a peaceful rock-eater. It is very thin but broad (about 10’ × 10’ × 3”), and tunnels through solid rock at 1’ per week, slowly wearing it away. Usually a male and a female tunnel near each other. They avoid metal, detouring around even small deposits, so their tunnels wander.

Because they look like stone, smell repulsive, and are indigestible, flesh-eaters rarely bother them.

Eggs: in her 1,000-year life a female ovulates only once. If a male is nearby (one usually is), she lays 3-8 eggs that hatch in 100 years. The eggs look like ordinary fist-sized stones and are not laid together; the chance of finding one in an area a female frequents is 1 in 1,000. Certain wealthy mine-owners will pay 1,000 gold pieces or more for an egg.

system.description:
(*The X.P. value is for destroying its Material Plane form only; if it is actually killed permanently, multiply it by 10.)

Styx devils live on the fifth plane of Hell. They are humanoid, with disproportionately large, ugly heads and black wings trimmed with silver. Their main task is to find souls to take back to Geryon, but from time to time they tour the Material Plane intent on destroying every human they meet. They are manoeuvrability class C in aerial combat.

  • Defences: ordinary weapons cannot harm them; silver weapons and magical weapons of +1 or better can.
  • Touch: 2-8 hit points of damage, with a 50% chance of an imprisonment spell on the victim (no saving throw). Treat it as cast at the 22nd level of magic use, with the devil knowing the victim’s name and background perfectly.
  • Dispelling a styx devil requires a holy word.

Devils: general (FF)

(Full details of devils are in the MM. The edited details that apply to the styx devil are reprinted here.)

  • Hierarchy: devils follow a strict chain of command, which they dare not break for fear of the arch-devils. Even so, there is great rivalry, even open hostility, between the devils of different planes and between the arch-devils.
  • Planes: all devils can move about the Planes of Hell (though only the dukes dare do so without authorisation), and to Gehenna, Hades, and Acheron at will. They can also travel the Astral Plane, though they seldom do. No devil can enter other planes unless the proper ritual is performed, a gate is opened, or a devil’s proper name is spoken (and heard).
  • Death: the material form of a greater devil or duke of Hell can be destroyed, but it cannot actually be slain except in Hell or the Lower Planes next to it. A greater devil whose material form is destroyed is reduced to a lemure for nine decades of torment before it resumes its former station (see the MM, Devil, Lemure).
  • Fighting: devils can never be subdued. Lesser devils always fight until destroyed; greater ones will negotiate if seriously threatened. All devils can split their attacks between two or more opponents if they have the means.
  • Service: devils will serve if properly commanded, but it is risky, since an improper command breaks the law that binds them (and it usually requires a contract for the commander’s soul). Persons other than lawful evil ones may summon or deal with devils (but had better use the proverbial long spoon when supping with them). Properly drawn magic circles keep devils off for a time (with symbols added for greater and arch-devils). Devils are repelled by holy (good) artifacts or relics.

Powers: all devils have or can use charm person, suggestion, illusion, infravision, teleportation (no error), know alignment, cause fear (effect varies), and animate dead. They can summon their fellows, much like a monster summoning spell. A special form of telepathy lets them understand and speak with any intelligent creature.

Attack forms: devils take damage from these as shown:

AttackMaximum damage will be
acidfull

fire (dragon, magical)none
gas (poisonous, etc.)half
iron weaponnone*
magic missilefull
poisonfull
silver weaponfull

* Unless the devil is affected by normal weapons, in which case damage is by weapon type.

Devils’ talismans: greater devils have a special combination of inscriptions that binds them to whoever wields it. Any devil’s talisman must be used with great care. Evil creatures using one must make a human sacrifice. Even looking at one is dangerous without the protection of spells or a magic circle: studying it gives a 10% chance of summoning the kind of devil, or the specific devil, it belongs to. Speaking the name on it always calls that devil forth.

Devil dogs are stark white hounds with blue eyes that live in cold regions. In snow- or frost-covered areas they are invisible beyond 30’. They roam in packs, endlessly searching for food, and always attack human parties, slyly making the most of their protective colouring.

  • Bite: it always leaps for the throat, normally doing 2-8 hit points. If the to-hit roll beats the score needed by 4 or more, or is a natural 20, it hits the throat: double damage, and the victim is comatose for 2-8 turns and dies at the end of that time unless he receives cure light wounds (or stronger healing of that kind) during it. (The bite itself may of course kill him anyway.)
  • Baying: when attacking or chasing, they give an intense baying that causes fear in any character of 3rd level or lower who fails a save against magic at −4.
  • Speed: they are very fast and can keep up their 30” rate for three turns, then must “rest” for three turns at no more than 12”.

Dire corbies are an underground race of huge black birds that walk upright. They are ferocious fighters that never need to check morale, always attacking and fighting to the death. Long ago they lost the power of flight, but they make up for it with great strength and ferocity. Their former wings are now two powerful arms ending in sharp, rock-hard claws, each doing 1-6 hit points of damage.

They hunt in flocks, running down their victims while giving horrifying shrieks. They have a crude language; those familiar with it recognise their attack cry as “Doom! Doom!”

They live in large underground caverns. They were once at open war with giant bats, but this has become an uneasy truce.

system.specialDefenses: Can only be hit by magical weapons
system.description:
The disenchanter looks like a spindly, camel-like animal with a long, flexible, muscular snout that can reach as much as 5’ from its head when it attacks. It is pale electric blue and slightly translucent, and may even be seen to shimmer.

  • Feeding: it can detect magic (in magical armour, shields, swords, and the like) and lives on the power of such enchantments. It is fairly discerning; it can tell armour of etherealness from +7 armour, for instance, and picks the former as the stronger. Meeting a party, it detects the most powerful magic item there and tries to fasten its snout onto it. A hit drains the magic, leaving the item unmarked but non-magical.
  • Referee’s judgement: consider how easily it could reach a particular item, despite its nimble snout. Generally it goes for an easy target, such as a magical shield within easy reach, rather than a more powerful item hidden in a backpack or sheath.
  • Defence: only magical weapons can hit it, and they do not lose their enchantment by doing so; it disenchants only with its snout.

No one has ever found a disenchanter’s lair or proved anything about its metabolism, which is curious to say the least.

The doombat is a monstrous black giant bat of dismal underground caverns, with a full 25’ wingspan. It can carry off up to 300 pounds (3,000 gold pieces weight). At night it flies out to hunt, always attacking and trying to kill any living thing. It is manoeuvrability class C in aerial combat.

  • Attacks: a bite for 1-6 hit points, and a lash of its barbed tail for 1-4. The tail reaches a good distance from the body; tails up to 12’ long have been reported.
  • Shriek: an ordinary bat’s sonar squeak has become a terrifying shriek of great sonic power. Each doombat can shriek continuously for 2-5 rounds, during which no one within 100’ who can hear it can concentrate: spell use is impossible and all attacks are at −1. There is no saving throw. Several doombats shrieking at once do not add together.
  • Light: bright light (such as a light spell) keeps a doombat at bay, though torch- or lantern-light does not deter it.

system.xp: 7HD: VI/575 + 8 per hit point; 8HD: VI/925 + 10 per hit point; 9HD: VII/1,400 + 12 per hit point
system.description:
The only oriental dragon with wings, the li lung has a lion’s body and a dragon’s head with human features. It lives underground and can swim, though it cannot breathe water. It is manoeuvrability class E in the air.

  • Attacks: two claws for 2-8 hit points each and a bite for 1-20.
  • Earthquake: it has no breath weapon, but once a day it can cause an earthquake (as the spell, but it cannot be dispelled), with a width and length in tens of feet equal to three times its age level; a sub-adult’s covers 30’ square. This may bring down the cavern the dragon lives in, but no earthquake ever harms a li lung (though it may have the inconvenience of digging itself out of the rubble).
  • Burrowing: its powerful claws dig through solid stone at 1” per turn, and through earth six times as fast.

Dragons, Oriental: general (FF)

Oriental dragons are related to other dragons but differ in some ways. Individuals vary in colour: white, red, yellow, blue, green, or black. Their powers depend on their type, and each kind is described separately; this section covers what they share.

Size: like other dragons, they come in three sizes (small, average, and huge). Roll d8: 1-2 small, 3-7 average, 8 huge. Size also sets the dragon’s number of hit dice.

Age: like other dragons, they pass through eight ages. Roll d8 for the age, which sets the hit points per die:

d8AgeYearsHit points per die
1Very young1-51
2Young6-152
3Sub-adult16-253
4Young adult26-504
5Adult51-1005
6Old101-2006
7Very old201-4007

system.hpNote: Rolling sets the dragon's hit dice (attack column) and, at 5 or more hit points per die, saves as total hit points ÷ 4 (rounded down) hit dice (FF p.28).

system.description:
Dragonfish are 2’ long, mottled brown flatfish that lie on the bottom of shallow fresh-water pools or slow streams and rivers. They blend in so well that they are very hard to spot (15% chance, even for searchers who know what they are looking for).

  • Spines: a fringe of horny, poison-tipped spines snaps off in anyone who steps or puts a hand on them. The poison is highly toxic (save at −1), and the spines are strong enough to pierce leather boots. The spines do no damage apart from the poison.
  • Bite: in melee a dragonfish bites for 1-6 hit points.

The dune stalker looks like a vile, naked, bony human with long, sharp fingers and clawed toes. It roams desert areas when summoned by high-level evil magicians, and attacks only good characters (any alignment that includes good draws its attack). Once set on a mission, it tracks without fail, like an invisible stalker (see the MM, Invisible Stalker). Only magical weapons can harm it.

  • Sonic attack: its usual attack is a sonic vibration with a range of 60’, doing 2-12 hit points to a single target (no saving throw).
  • Kiss of death: at close quarters it can press its lips to a victim’s skin, setting up vibrations so intense that the victim dies instantly unless he saves versus spells. A successful save cancels the effect.

Cryonax looks like a 15’ tall yeti with suckered tentacles instead of arms. He lives in a huge castle of ice, quartz, and glass where the Planes of Air and Water meet, drawing power from the Negative Material Plane.

  • Cold aura: he constantly radiates 1-6 points of cold damage to everyone within 15’ (those resistant to cold take half; there is no saving throw as such).
  • Attacks: he attacks as a 20 hit dice monster with two tentacles, each doing 5-20 hit points; the victim must also save versus paralysation or be frozen in place for 3-12 full turns.
  • Weapons: only +2 or better weapons damage him. There is a cumulative 10% chance that any particular weapon hitting him shatters, in which case that hit does no damage.
  • Summoning (once a day): 1-4 white dragons, 1-4 frost giants, or 1-6 yeti.
  • Three times a day: a triple-strength wall of ice, hold person, and an ice storm of 4-40 points.
  • Once a day: a 15-dice blast of cold.
  • Vulnerabilities and immunities: fire attacks against him are +2 to hit and do 1 extra point per attack die. Cold attacks add to his hit points by the damage they would have done, up to but not beyond his original 90 hit points. He is completely immune to poison and cannot be turned to stone.

Elemental Princes of Evil: general (FF)

The princes of evil air, cold, earth, fire, and water creatures are powerful beings who rule mainly on the Elemental Planes but also have many followers on the Prime Material Plane. They are often at odds with one another (mostly through their underlings’ doings), but share these powers:

  • At will: detect invisible, dispel magic (at 20th level), infravision (lasting one day), know alignment, suggestion (lasting 12 hours), and teleportation (no error).
  • Telepathy: a special telepathic power lets them understand and speak with any intelligent creature.
  • Three times a day each: read languages and read magic.
  • Once a day: telekinesis of 6,000 gold pieces weight.

Each prince’s experience point value is for destroying its material form only. If a prince is killed permanently, multiply it by 10.

Imix usually appears as an 18’ high pillar of fire. He lives deep in a monstrous active volcano on the Elemental Plane of Fire, and there is great enmity between him and Olhydra.

  • Heat aura: he constantly radiates 1-20 points of heat damage to everyone within 10’ (those resistant to fire take half; there is no saving throw as such).
  • Attack: once per round as a 20 hit dice creature, for 6-36 hit points. Only +2 or better weapons can harm him.
  • Summoning (once a day): 1-3 efreet, 1-3 fire elementals, or 1-3 salamanders.
  • Three times a day: painfully bright continual light, a triple-strength wall of fire, and pyrotechnics.
  • Once a day: a 20-dice fireball.
  • Vulnerabilities and immunities: water attacks on him are +1 to hit; cold attacks are +2 to hit and do 1 extra point per attack die. He is immune to paralysis, poison, and petrifaction.

  • Telepathy: a special telepathic power lets them understand and speak with any intelligent creature.
  • Three times a day each: read languages and read magic.
  • Once a day: telekinesis of 6,000 gold pieces weight.

Each prince’s experience point value is for destroying its material form only. If a prince is killed permanently, multiply it by 10.

Ogrémoch appears as a rough, seemingly unfinished two-legged figure 10’ tall. He lives in a great flat-topped mountain on the Elemental Plane of Earth.

  • Attacks: as a 24 hit dice monster, two strikes each round for 5-50 hit points each. Only +3 or better weapons can harm him.
  • Summoning (once a day): 1-3 earth elementals, 1-6 evil khargra, 1-4 umber hulks, or 1-4 evil xorn.
  • Three times a day: a triple-strength wall of stone, move earth (double area, casting time in rounds instead of turns), and flesh to stone.
  • Once a day: an earthquake 100’ across.
  • Defences: normal fire and poison cannot harm him. Cold, lightning, and magical fire do 1 point less per attack die.

  • Telepathy: a special telepathic power lets them understand and speak with any intelligent creature.
  • Three times a day each: read languages and read magic.
  • Once a day: telekinesis of 6,000 gold pieces weight.

Each prince’s experience point value is for destroying its material form only. If a prince is killed permanently, multiply it by 10.

Olhydra appears only near water, as a watery, shapeless blob 20’ across. She lives in a great undersea castle on the Elemental Plane of Water, and there is great enmity between her and Imix.

  • Wave: once per round she attacks as a 20 hit dice monster with a water wave doing 2-24 points of damage.
  • Engulfing: she can also engulf and drown up to five human-sized creatures at once. All defenders count as armour class 6 against this (with magical and dexterity adjustments). Engulfed victims can do nothing (fight, cast spells), take 2-12 hit points each round, and drown in 2-8 rounds. She cannot move engulfed bodies, so the only way to save them is to kill or drive her off.
  • Ramming: she can ram ships with the force of two heavy galleys.
  • Weapons: only +1 or better weapons can hit her, and edged weapons do only half damage.
  • Summoning (once a day): 1-3 water elementals, 1-2 sea hags, 2-5 water weirds, or 20-200 sahuagin (salt water only).
  • Three times a day: a triple-strength wall of fog, lower water and part water (at 20th level), transmute rock to mud, and ice storm.
  • Fire and cold: fire attacks against her are +2 to hit and do 1 extra point per attack die. Any normal fire within 10’ of her goes out automatically. Cold cannot damage her, but cold of more than 20 points acts as a slow spell on her (her magic resistance does not apply and she gets no saving throw).
  • She cannot be paralysed or turned to stone.

Each prince’s experience point value is for destroying its material form only. If a prince is killed permanently, multiply it by 10.

Yan-C-Bin is naturally invisible, but makes a slight disturbance in the air as he flies, which high-level characters may detect (see the DMG, Invisibility). He is about 10’ across with no definite shape, and lives in a great airy palace on the Elemental Plane of Air. He is manoeuvrability class A in aerial combat.

  • Attacks: as a 19 hit dice monster, twice per round for 2-20 hit points each, with the same chance as an 8th-level monk to stun or kill outright. Only +2 or better weapons can harm him.
  • Summoning (once a day): 1-3 air elementals, 1-4 cloud giants, 1-4 invisible stalkers, or 1-3 wind walkers.
  • Defences: lightning has no effect on him, and no object thrown into the air can harm him. He is immune to petrifaction. Fire attacks against him get +1 to hit for every four levels of the attacker (as printed: a 3rd-level character gets +1, a seventh-level character +2, and so on).
  • Whirlwind: he can become a whirlwind shaped like an upside-down cone with its tip cut off: 2” across at the bottom, 6” across at the top, and 16” high. If an overhead obstruction keeps it from its full height, it is only half strength. At full strength it sweeps away and kills all creatures under three hit dice and does 4-32 hit points to every non-aerial creature it does not kill outright; at half strength it does 2-16. He can keep this form for 2-5 rounds, and forming or dissolving it takes a full round.
